implementation_notes: Swift's standard toolchain has no reflection and no dynamic mock generator, so the idiomatic realization is a small test-only type that conforms to the collaborator's protocol (or to a protocol extracted for the test) and records the calls it receives in properties while returning programmed values - Meszaros' Hand-Built Test Double, with assertions on the recording after the exercise. Cuckoo generates Mockito-style mocks from a compile-time crawl of your sources, but it cannot mock structs, final types or statics, so protocol extraction stays the baseline and a hand-written double is often clearer when only one or two interactions matter.
pitfalls: A protocol extension that supplies a default implementation satisfies the mock without recording anything; keep recorded requirements abstract so the test double must implement them.
Recording state must live in a reference type: a struct double is copied when handed to the SUT, so the test sees no calls.
final classes, structs and value types cannot be subclassed or intercepted - extract a protocol and mock that instead of forcing the real type into a double.
